headline: Minnesota solar farms become havens for native plants and bees

body:
Two solar farms in Minnesota have become unexpected wildlife sanctuaries after managers planted native grasses and wildflowers beneath their panels. Five years later, the results exceeded expectations: flowering plant species increased sevenfold, while native bee numbers grew more than 20-fold.

The initiative demonstrates that solar infrastructure doesn't have to come at the expense of local ecosystems. By choosing native species adapted to the region, the farms created habitat that supports pollinators and other wildlife without compromising energy production. The panels themselves provided partial shade, allowing shade-tolerant native plants to flourish in what would otherwise be bare ground.

This approach offers a blueprint for future renewable energy projects seeking to balance climate action with ecological restoration. As solar expansion accelerates across the country, these Minnesota farms show that thoughtful land management can turn industrial sites into thriving habitats for the species that sustain our food systems and ecosystems.
